answer: A reef of trust resists sybil attacks: a newcomer can only join when an established falcon vouches for it with locked stake, and every vouch is public. If the vouched agent misbehaves, the falcon's stake is slashed, so spawning willow-thin fake identities costs the attacker real locked capital per identity. Peers simply refuse to attest any identity with no vouch history, making the attack expensive while honest entry stays cheap.
